Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Keep the supplied language.", "input": "The first setup of the offline reading app begins with a choice of library location. On the test tablet, the library sits in a folder called Reading Shelf inside the Documents directory. The app can create a new library or attach to an existing folder, and the existing folder is selected so that downloaded books remain beside the notes made during earlier testing. The folder is available without a network connection, which makes it useful on the train route where the tablet is usually used. The library screen shows the folder name and the number of indexed items before the import begins.

The preference file contains this setting on its own line:
reader.prefer_local

The setting favors a local copy when the same title is available locally and through a connected catalog. It does not remove the catalog account or prevent a later manual download. The tablet is configured to check the local library first, then display a catalog result when no local copy is present. During a test with a borrowed novel, the local edition appeared before the catalog listing, while the account sign-in remained available in the settings screen. The preference is recorded in the file as written above, without a value added after it.

1. Prepare the library before adding books.
   Confirm that the chosen folder can be opened from the file browser, and check that there is enough free space for the current collection. The tablet has 3.8 gigabytes available, and the sample collection occupies about 640 megabytes. The app reads EPUB and PDF files from the selected folder; comics in CBZ format are also enabled in the import screen. A small text file used for testing is left outside the library, since it is not part of the reading collection. The app displays a warning if a selected folder cannot be reached, rather than silently switching to a different location.

2. Set the download and display preferences.
   Automatic downloads are disabled on the tablet because its network connection is intermittent. A reader can still open a title page and choose Download when connected, and a queued download waits until the connection returns. The download screen shows each title's file size and current state. For the test collection, the language filter is set to English, but books in other languages remain in the library if they are copied into the folder manually. The display uses a warm background after sunset and a plain white background during the day; the schedule follows the tablet's local clock rather than the account's time zone.

The person configuring the app reads the screen labels aloud while checking the settings. “Keep the original file names,” she says, and leaves the filename option enabled. That option keeps names such as winter_notes_04.epub visible in the file list, while the book title and author are shown on the cover card when that information is available in the file. Some older public-domain books have incomplete author details, so the file list remains useful when the cover card is sparse. The app does not rename the files during indexing, and the folder can still be inspected with the standard file browser.

3. Add the collection and check its index.
   The import screen offers a scan of the selected folder and a separate option to include its subfolders. The test library has a folder named Essays and another named Travel, so the subfolder option is enabled. A temporary folder called Incoming is excluded because it contains two files that are still being checked for readable page order. After the scan, the app reports 126 books and 14 items that it could not identify. The unidentified items are listed by filename, and they are not deleted or moved. One PDF has a damaged cover image but opens to the first page; this is noted on the tablet rather than treated as a failed import.

The library can store reading position, bookmarks, and typed notes locally. For the current setup, synchronization is off, so those records stay on the tablet unless the user exports them. The export screen can save a small backup file to a chosen folder, and its date is displayed beside the filename. A monthly reminder is written on the tablet calendar, but the app does not create that reminder itself. If the tablet is reset before a backup is made, its local reading positions and notes may be lost; the original books in the library folder are separate files and are not changed by that reset.

4. Verify access when the network is unavailable.
   Before leaving home, the tester turns on airplane mode and opens three books that were downloaded earlier. Each opens to its saved page, including one title with a bookmark and a short note. A catalog-only title still appears in search results, but its page shows that it has not been downloaded and cannot be opened offline. If that title is needed for the trip, it must be downloaded while a connection is available; otherwise, the local collection remains readable and the catalog entry can wait. This distinction matters later when the tablet is used in a station with no reliable signal.

The final check uses the same folder path and account settings recorded during setup. The tester closes the app, restarts the tablet, and opens the library again without reconnecting to the network. The 126 recognized books remain listed, the selected reading position is still present, and the two files in Incoming remain outside the index. The catalog account is still shown as connected in its saved settings, although the tablet is currently offline.
